cases.purpose: rfc5011-poll fetches the apex DNSKEY RRset from a loopback server and drives one rollover step per poll at injected --now values (add pending, still pending, promote) (r4).
cases.oracle: RFC 5011 s2.4.1 add/promote hold-down semantics and RFC 4034 Appendix B key tags (checked against the RFC 4034 s5.4 example tag 60485) computed independently in Python; the primary is a Python UDP DNSKEY responder that also records the queries it saw.
cases.comparison: Three candidate polls at --now 1000/1050/1100 with --hold-down 100 against a loopback responder returning keys K1 (already active) and K2 (new); the helper checks the printed transitions, the active/previous/candidate anchor files and that the server saw three DNSKEY queries for the zone.
cases.script:
H=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w2-dnskey.py
export BASHDNS_SERVER_PORT=5390
exec 7<>w.fifo
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" serve 5390 ready 2> serve.err &
srv=$!
for i in {1..100}; do [[ -e ready ]] && break; read -t 0.05 -u 7 l; done
for t in 1000 1050 1100; do
  dns rfc5011-poll --anchor-dir anchors --zone rollover.test -s 127.0.0.1 --now $t --hold-down 100 > out-$t.txt 2> err-$t.txt
  echo "$?" >> rcs.txt
done
kill "$srv"; wait "$srv" 2>/dev/null
/usr/bin/python3 "$H" verify
